name: mid-devops-sre-bengaluru
note: Three and a half years SRE with genuine incident and cost numbers, against a platform SRE posting at a fintech in the same city. Strong match. Kubernetes, Terraform and observability all line up; the gap is service mesh and Go.
resume_text:
Arjun Reddy
Site Reliability Engineer | Bengaluru, India
arjun.reddy@example.com | +91 98450 30277 | github.com/arjunreddy-sre

SUMMARY
SRE with three and a half years keeping a mid-sized e-commerce platform up. Most of my work
is Kubernetes, Terraform and the unglamorous business of making alerts mean something.

EXPERIENCE

Kettl Commerce - Site Reliability Engineer
Bengaluru | Feb 2023 - Present
- Run the production Kubernetes estate: 3 EKS clusters, 62 services, around 400 pods at
  peak on sale days.
- Migrated 41 of 62 services from hand-rolled Helm charts to a shared chart library,
  cutting the average new-service onboarding from two days to about three hours.
- Wrote the Terraform modules for VPC, EKS, RDS and IAM that all three environments now
  use. Before this, staging and production had drifted far enough that a staging pass told
  you almost nothing.
- Cut monthly AWS spend by 31% (roughly 14 lakh INR a year) through rightsizing node
  groups, moving batch workloads to Spot, and deleting 2.1TB of orphaned EBS snapshots.
- Rebuilt alerting in Prometheus and Alertmanager around symptom-based SLO burn rate
  alerts. Pages per week went from about 40, most of them ignorable, to 6.
- Reduced mean time to recovery on P1 incidents from 68 minutes to 24 minutes over three
  quarters, mostly by writing runbooks during the postmortem instead of promising to.
- Introduced blameless postmortems. 23 written so far, and the action items are tracked in
  the same board as feature work rather than in a document nobody reopens.
- Built the CI pipeline in GitHub Actions and Argo CD that took deploys from a Friday
  afternoon ritual to on-demand, averaging 19 production deploys a week.

Insightwave Analytics - DevOps Engineer
Hyderabad | Jun 2021 - Jan 2023
- Containerised 12 legacy Java services and moved them from EC2 to ECS.
- Set up the ELK stack for centralised logging across 30 hosts.
- Automated nightly RDS snapshot verification with a Lambda that restored to a scratch
  instance and ran a checksum, which caught two silently broken backups in the first month.
- Maintained Jenkins pipelines and migrated 18 of them to declarative syntax.

EDUCATION
B.Tech Electronics and Communication Engineering
Vellore Institute of Technology, 2017 - 2021

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), 2023
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate, 2022

SKILLS
Orchestration: Kubernetes, EKS, Helm, Argo CD, Docker
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Terragrunt, Ansible
Cloud: AWS (EKS, EC2, RDS, S3, IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch, VPC)
Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, Loki, ELK
CI/CD: GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Argo CD
Scripting: Python, Bash
Practices: SLOs, error budgets, incident command, blameless postmortems, on-call
jd_text:
Site Reliability Engineer II - Platform
Bengaluru (Hybrid) | Infrastructure

We are a payments company. When we are down, merchants cannot take money, so reliability is
not an internal quality metric here, it is the product. The platform group is nine engineers
and owns the Kubernetes estate, the deployment path and the observability stack that the
forty product engineers build on top of.

What you will own
- Our production Kubernetes clusters on EKS, including upgrades, capacity and the node
  group strategy
- The Terraform codebase that describes every environment. We have no click-ops and we
  intend to keep it that way
- The golden path for deployment: Helm charts, Argo CD, and the progressive delivery setup
  that product teams use without needing to understand it
- Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, and increasingly OpenTelemetry tracing
- SLO definition with product teams, and the error budget conversations that follow
- Participation in the follow-the-sun on-call rotation, roughly one week in six

Requirements
- 3 to 6 years in SRE, DevOps or platform engineering, with at least two of those running
  Kubernetes in production rather than in a lab
- Terraform at module-authoring level. You should have opinions about state layout
- Deep AWS: VPC design, IAM, EKS, RDS
- Prometheus and Grafana, and specifically the difference between alerting on symptoms and
  alerting on causes
- Experience being on-call for something that mattered, and having run or written at least
  one postmortem you are not embarrassed by
- Linux fundamentals and confident Bash or Python scripting
- CI/CD ownership, not just pipeline usage

Highly desirable
- Go. Our internal tooling is written in it and we would like you to contribute
- A service mesh in production, Istio or Linkerd
- OpenTelemetry instrumentation across polyglot services
- Kubernetes operators, or any controller-runtime work
- Cost optimisation at a scale where the savings were worth reporting
- CKA or CKS
- Regulated environment experience: PCI DSS, RBI guidelines, audit evidence

What we do not need
Windows administration, VMware, or on-prem datacentre work. We are cloud native and have
been since day one.

Compensation: 28 to 42 LPA plus ESOPs, depending on level. Hybrid, three days a week in the
Indiranagar office.
